chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him)
That he disliked what the bird ate of carrion.

key_terms.الْجِيفَةَ: Carrion (dead animals not slaughtered according to ritual law)
key_terms.كَرِهَ: Disliked (indicating a legal preference or mild prohibition, not absolute haram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on birds that eat carrion in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on birds that consume carrion (al-jifah), indicating that their meat is either makruh (disliked) or requires specific consideration due to their diet. In Shia fiqh, this highlights the principle that the dietary habits of animals can influence the permissibility or quality of their meat, distinguishing them from those fed on clean sustenance. This view is often contextualized within the broader discussion of 'dhabihah' (ritual slaughter) versus natural consumption for birds.
